threads.body: [Testing] Reduced-mode filtering currently applies to JettyJpmsSmokeTest as an “other server”, which means only the minimum JDK (11) will run for Jetty JPMS. This contradicts the PR description/previous intent (“JPMS … unchanged”) and drops the multi-JDK JPMS coverage on PR builds.

threads.body: [Testing] In reduced-smoke-tests mode, AppServerTest forces TomEE to run openj9 only, but the workflow still passes -PskipOpenJ9SmokeTests=true on PRs by default. That combination results in the Tomee suite running zero tests (all hotspot tests assumed away; all Openj9 tests excluded by Gradle), which defeats the stated goal of keeping an OpenJ9 signal via TomEE.

replies.body: Good catch. I also fixed the reduced-mode OpenJ9 interaction so PR reduced smoke runs no longer pass `-PskipOpenJ9SmokeTests=true`, which keeps the intended TomEE OpenJ9 representative coverage.

threads.body:
[General] Two things.

**1. `!inputs.reduced-smoke-tests` is load-bearing but looks removable.** It can't be dropped: on a normal PR both flags are on, `-PskipOpenJ9SmokeTests=true` excludes `**/*Openj9*.*`, and the reduced rule skips TomEE hotspot — so the `tomee` suite would run **zero** tests. Please add a one-line comment saying reduced mode owns the openj9 policy, otherwise someone will "simplify" this later and silently lose a whole suite.

**2. Cost/benefit — I'm not convinced this earns its complexity.** I counted the `@AppServer` classes actually selected in each mode:

| suite | full matrix | PR today | PR with this change |
|---|---|---|---|
| jetty | 36 | 20 | 8 |
| liberty | 38 | 21 | 9 |
| payara | 13 | 6 | 3 |
| **tomcat** | 30 | **15** | **15** |
| **tomee** | 22 | **11** | **11** |
| websphere | 2 | 2 | 2 |
| wildfly | 36 | 18 | 6 |
| **total** | 177 | 93 | 54 |

The two suites named as the coverage anchors are the two that don't shrink at all. Tomcat is already hotspot-only on PRs, so "Tomcat covers all JDKs on hotspot" is exactly today's behavior. TomEE keeps the same 11 containers but flips them from hotspot to openj9, which are the slower images. openj9 containers on a normal PR go from **2 to 13**.

And the wall-clock argument doesn't hold. From a recent `build-pull-request` run (`30482654548`):

```
build / common / build                              26.8 min   <- critical path
build / common / test0 (26, hotspot, indy true)     23.0
build / common / smoke-test (liberty)               22.3
build / common / smoke-test (other)                 20.4       <- not touched by this PR
build / common / smoke-test (wildfly)               15.5
build / common / smoke-test (jetty)                 14.8
build / common / smoke-test (payara)                13.2
build / common / smoke-test (tomcat)                10.8
build / common / smoke-test (websphere)              9.6
build / common / smoke-test (tomee)                  9.6
run wall clock                                      27.7 min
```

`smoke-test` has no `needs:`, so it runs concurrently with everything else and `build` at 26.8 min sets the critical path. Even deleting every servlet smoke test saves ~0 min of PR feedback time, and within the smoke stage the untouched non-servlet `other` suite already floors it at 20.4 min.

So the real benefit is runner minutes (and less flake surface), not faster PRs. That may well be worth having — but the PR description should say that, with numbers, and drop the implication that PR builds get faster. If wall clock is the actual goal, the levers are `build` and the `other` smoke suite, not this matrix.

replies.body: Addressed in a2b9c36: added the load-bearing guard explanation and updated the PR description with 177 full / 93 current PR / 54 reduced combinations, invocation and Gradle-time measurements, and the runner-minute/flake benefit rather than a wall-clock claim.

threads.body:
[General] This makes the `test openj9` label a no-op on its own.

With only `test openj9` applied: `skip-openj9-tests` becomes false, but `reduced-smoke-tests` is still true, so `skipIfNotReduced` still clamps openj9 down to TomEE only. You'd need `test openj9` **and** `test full smoke` to get what `test openj9` alone gives on `main` today. That's a silent regression for anyone using the label to debug an openj9-specific failure.

```suggestion
      reduced-smoke-tests: ${{ !contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'test full smoke') && !contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'test openj9') }}
```

Separately, `.github/workflows/comment-on-test-label.yml` posts the "labels don't retrigger the build" reminder, but its `if:` (lines 26-27) only matches `test openj9` / `test windows`. `test full smoke` has exactly the same footgun, so it needs to be added there too:

```yaml
    if: |
      github.event.label.name == 'test openj9' ||
      github.event.label.name == 'test windows' ||
      github.event.label.name == 'test full smoke'
```

threads.body:
[Testing] Concerns with this block, in rough priority order:

1. `AppServerTest` now `instanceof`-tests four of its own subclasses. That's an inverted dependency in a base class, and the failure mode is quiet: a newly added app server falls through to "hotspot only, minimum JDK per version" without anyone deciding that.
2. Selecting the **minimum** JDK per version biases PR coverage toward the oldest JDK. After this change, JDK 21/25 on Wildfly, Liberty, Payara and Jetty is not exercised on PRs at all — only Tomcat and Jetty JPMS cover new JDKs. Newer JDKs are where servlet-container regressions usually show up, so max JDK would likely catch more per container started.
3. `getClass().getEnclosingClass()` on line 97 NPEs for any top-level `@AppServer` class. Every one is nested today, so it isn't a live bug, but nothing enforces that.
4. The `JettyJpmsSmokeTest` and `WebsphereSmokeTest` branches are pure no-ops — both fall through to `return` with no assumption. They read as policy but do nothing.
5. `skipIfNotReduced` reads backwards: it skips when reduced mode is **on** and the case is not in the reduced set. `assumeInReducedMatrix` or similar would say what it does.

All of it goes away with the `@AppServer(reduced = true)` approach from my previous comment:

```suggestion
```

replies.body: Addressed in a2b9c36: removed the reflection, subclass checks, minimum-JDK derivation, and quiet fallback; reduced-matrix membership is now explicit beside each matrix entry.

[Naming] Only the app-server suites shrink here, since `AppServerTest` is the sole reader, so `smokeTests` overclaims and the `other` suite is untouched. One spelling from label to assumption would read better:

| concept | now | suggested |
|---|---|---|
| workflow input | `reduced-smoke-tests` | `reduced-appserver-tests` |
| Gradle property | `-PreducedSmokeTests` | `-PreducedAppServerTests` |
| system property | `reducedSmokeTests` | `reducedAppServerTests` |
| annotation attribute | `reduced` | `inReducedMatrix` |

I'd keep "matrix" out of the workflow input, because `strategy.matrix` sits in the same job, and keep it on the annotation, where `reduced` describes the entry rather than its membership.
